state.persist_today: persist_layout (shared by place and rate) rewrites ~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua from the monitors connected right now, keyed by port name (output = "HDMI-A-1"). A rule for a monitor that is unplugged at that moment is dropped, so a laptop user who sets 75 Hz on the office monitor, changes anything at home, and comes back gets the monitor's default mode and position again. Port keys also mean any display plugged into that port inherits the rule: a classroom projector on HDMI-A-1 is asked for 1920x1080@74.97 at scale 1.25.

Hyprland monitor rules accept a desc: selector (hyprlang monitor=desc:...); the Lua form output = "desc:..." is expected to match the same way, to be verified in the nested harness. macOS and Windows remember display settings per display, not per port.
state.labels: Pills show the exact rate to two decimals: '74.97 Hz', '60 Hz', '59.94 Hz'. Windows 11 lists exact decimals; people buy a '75 Hz monitor'. Rounding is safe only when no two listed rates round to the same integer (60 and 59.94 do).
state.safety: koompi-displays checks only that the compositor reports the new rate, then saves at once. A rate the EDID lists but the cable, adapter or projector cannot carry leaves a black screen, and the saved rule brings it back at every login. Windows, macOS (for resolution), GNOME and KDE all ask 'Keep these display settings?' and revert after 15 to 20 s without an answer.

J16_persist_scope.instructions: How should saved monitor rules be keyed and kept?

criteria.desc_keyed_merge: Key each saved rule by the monitor's description (desc:), and keep rules for monitors that are not connected. Strongest case: per-display memory like macOS and Windows; a projector on the same port never inherits another display's mode and scale; unplugging never loses a setting. Cost: merging with the old file, and proving desc: matching in Lua.
criteria.port_keyed_merge: Keep port names, and keep rules for ports that are not connected. Strongest case: smaller change. Cost: any display on that port still inherits the rule.
criteria.leave: Leave it as place always did. Cost: settings vanish after a change made while a monitor is unplugged.

J16_rate_labels.instructions: How should the refresh-rate pills be labelled?

criteria.round_unless_ambiguous: Whole hertz ('75 Hz', '60 Hz') unless two listed rates round to the same integer, then two decimals for those ('59.94 Hz'). Strongest case: matches what people bought, stays exact where it matters.
criteria.exact: Always the exact rate to two decimals, as now. Strongest case: no hidden rounding, like Windows 11.

J16_confirm_revert.instructions: Should a refresh-rate change ask to be kept?

criteria.confirm_or_revert: After the switch, ask 'Keep this refresh rate?' with a 15 s countdown; save only on Keep, revert to the previous rate on Revert or timeout. Strongest case: every major desktop does it, and a black screen fixes itself.
criteria.apply_directly: Keep applying and saving at once. Strongest case: one click. Cost: a rate the display cannot show leaves a black screen that survives reboot.
